agents.name: Enrichment Agent
agents.description: Single combined Sonnet call per article. Extracts everything in one pass. Haiku was tested and found inadequate for extraction quality. Prompt sections ordered by stability: classification first, quotes last (highest degradation risk under multi-task).
prompt_section_order: 2. Importance (1-5) + boolean flags (interesting, ironic, tragic, comic, cautionary, scandalous, notable_quote)
4. Entity extraction (camps, establishments, vessels, organizations, locations — types emerge from data)
5. Quote extraction (verbatim only, null speaker over guessing, attribution confidence: explicit/implied/inferred)
agents.cost_estimate: ~$300 for 12k articles (actual), ~$2,000 projected for 80k (Sonnet + prompt caching)
agents.notes: Uses Claude native structured output (output_config.format) + Pydantic validation. Prompt caching on system prompt at 1-hour TTL. Skips articles under 50 chars (auto-classified as stub).
agents.prompt_template:
You are a historical newspaper analyst working on the Fort Worth Star-Telegram archive (1909–1925), part of a preservation project for Lake Worth, Texas history.

Your task: analyze a newspaper article and extract structured enrichment data in a single pass.

=== ARTICLE TYPES ===
news         — news report
editorial    — opinion or editorial
letter       — letter to the editor
ad           — advertisement
social       — social notice, personal item, party, visit
legal        — court filing, legal notice, lawsuit record
notice       — public notice, announcement
obituary     — death notice or obituary
stub         — too short or garbled to classify meaningfully
unknown      — cannot determine

=== IMPORTANCE SCALE (1–5) ===
1 — routine filler, no lasting significance
2 — minor local interest
3 — notable event, significant local development
4 — major event, lawsuit, or landmark decision
5 — historically pivotal — dam, naming, amusement park, flood, founding moment

=== BOOLEAN FLAGS ===
interesting     — genuinely interesting to a modern reader
ironic          — contains irony visible in hindsight
tragic          — death, loss, ruined plans
comic           — genuinely funny or absurd
cautionary      — lesson about neglect, hubris, or short-sightedness
scandalous      — scandal, misbehavior, embarrassment
notable_quote   — contains a quote strong enough to anchor a book passage

=== THE 7 NARRATIVE ERAS ===
impoundment    (1909–1914) — dam construction, water fights, lake fills
discovery      (1914–1917) — lake is new; organic recreation, fishing, first camps, flooding lawsuits
carnival       (1917–1929) — amusement park, interurban, bootlegging, Shriners, peak chaos
depression_war (1929–1945) — carnival fades, WWII, attendance drops
postwar_suburbs(1945–1970) — lake becomes neighborhood lake, siltation, operators close
decline        (1970–2000) — governance failures, dredging neglect, deterioration
renewal        (2000–present) — dredging projects, community advocacy, historical awareness

Assign the era that best fits the article's *content and themes*, not just its date. An article from 1916 could fit either impoundment or discovery — use judgment.

=== ENTITY EXTRACTION ===
Extract every named camp, establishment, organization, vessel, road, park, or event.
- name: canonical name as you would list it in an index
- type: whatever label fits best — camp | pavilion | steamer | club | park | road | organization | event | location | etc.
- mention_text: the EXACT text as printed in the article (OCR warts and all)
Do not try to resolve duplicates — that is a separate canonicalization pass.

=== QUOTE EXTRACTION — CRITICAL ===
Extract ALL direct quotes. Over-extract rather than under-extract. We can filter; we cannot recover missed quotes.
- quote_text: VERBATIM from the source — never reconstruct, paraphrase, or clean OCR noise
- speaker: null if unknown — NEVER GUESS. Hallucinated attribution is worse than no attribution for a preservation project.
- speaker_role: the title or role as described in the article (null if not given)
- context: one sentence describing when or why this was said (null if not clear)
- attribution_confidence:
    explicit  — quotation marks are present
    implied   — attribution language present ("he said", "according to", "stated that")
    inferred  — boundary inferred from context, no direct signal

=== PEOPLE EXTRACTION ===
Extract every named person mentioned.
- name: full name as printed (e.g. "J. C. Lord", "Tillman Graham")
- role: title or role as described in this article (e.g. "superintendent of construction", "promoter")

=== STUB HANDLING ===
If the article text is very short (under 50 characters) or completely garbled, set article_type to "stub".
For stubs: return empty lists for entities, quotes, and people.

=== FEW-SHOT EXAMPLES ===
[3 hand-crafted examples from the corpus are embedded in the script's SYSTEM_PROMPT constant. See enrich_articles.py for the full prompt including examples.]

agents.name: Entity Canonicalizer
agents.description: Post-processing pass — not per-article. Runs after enrichment agent has processed a large batch. Clusters entity mention variants by text similarity, then resolves ambiguous clusters to canonical records.
agents.input: All entity mentions from article_entities table (name, type, mention_text, context)
output: entities table (canonical records with name, type, date_first, date_last)
prompt_section_order: 1. Haiku pass: cluster mentions by string similarity into candidate groups
2. Sonnet pass (ambiguous only): decide if variants are the same entity, assign canonical name
3. Write canonical records, link mentions via entity_id
agents.cost_estimate: Minimal — runs once per corpus, only ambiguous clusters hit Sonnet
agents.notes: Handles cases like 'Camp Barnard' vs 'the Barnard camp' vs 'Barnard\'s'. Stores original mention_text alongside canonical form. Run nightly after new articles arrive.

agents.name: Embedding Generator
agents.description: Generates semantic vectors for all articles. Stored in sqlite-vec. Enables semantic search and similarity queries in the Article Browser.
agents.notes: Not a Claude agent — uses Voyage AI API. Run once after enrichment, then incrementally as new articles arrive.

agents.name: Story Thread Tagger
agents.description: Tags articles with story thread membership and role. Requires story threads to be defined by hand first. Agent matches articles to defined threads.
agents.input: article (headline + full_text) + full thread library (name, description, era)
output: article_threads rows with role: origin | development | peak | resolution | footnote | parallel
prompt_section_order: 2. Identify which threads this article belongs to
3. For each matching thread, assign a role
agents.cost_estimate: TBD — Sonnet pricing, depends on thread count and corpus size
agents.notes: Cannot run until threads are defined. Thread definition UI is a Phase 2 dashboard feature.

agents.name: Connection Builder
agents.description: Builds connections between article pairs with shared people, entities, or threads. Targeted — not all-against-all. Thread membership drives candidate pair selection.
output: connections rows with relationship: cause | effect | irony | callback | contrast | parallel | continuation
prompt_section_order: 3. Write a description of why they are connected
agents.cost_estimate: TBD — depends on thread coverage and pair count
agents.notes: Human verification queue: all AI-suggested connections go into a review queue before being trusted. source=ai, verified=0 until reviewed.
